extracted.intended_audience: academic authors preparing responses to peer review comments (manuscript revision)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on how to read, prioritize, document, and respond to reviewers’ comments when revising a manuscript for journal publication, including ethical issues and use of tools. Emphasizes organization, professionalism, and when to consult editors or mentors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize feedback (major vs minor)
rubrics_metrics.description: In practice, authors are advised to categorize each reviewer comments into major and minor ones, focusing on major revisions that directly influence the study’s methodology, results, or conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach helps authors address the most critical issues first. Example major issues: requests to clarify data analysis or to include additional experiments. Minor issues include grammatical corrections or stylistic suggestions. Added text: "Prioritizing feedback: categorize reviewer comments into major and minor critiques, focusing on major revisions that directly impact the study’s methodology, results, or conclusions."

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professionalism and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Be polite and respectful of all reviewers; remain objective and do not personalize challenging critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond thoughtfully, acknowledge input, and avoid taking critique personally. Example phrasing: begin with thanks (e.g., “We thank the reviewer for their insightful feedback on our methodology”) and then provide a detailed explanation or respectful rebuttal supported by evidence. Reduce repetitive expressions of gratitude — a single well-crafted expression may be sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize responses clearly (use tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tables to organize responses to reviewers to present, clearly and systematically, how each comment was addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables allow editors and reviewers to easily follow changes made for each comment. The suggestion to use tables is recommended as it enables a clear, organized presentation of how each comment was addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek guidance when uncertain (editor or mentor)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an author is unsure how to address a particular comment, they can reach out to the editor or a mentor for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consulting the editor-in-chief or a mentor with expertise in the field provides clarity and helps ensure responses are appropriate. This is recommended for ambiguous or substantial requests where the correct course of action isn't clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle ambiguous or ethical situations appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: In ambiguous or potentially unethical situations (e.g., suspected undisclosed use of AI in a review), authors should alert the editors and follow established ethical guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to international resources and policies (e.g., Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE), International Committee of Medical Journal Editors) for handling conflicts of interest, suspected misconduct, and other ethical issues. The page specifically advises alerting editors if authors suspect a reviewer used AI-assisted technologies to produce a review report without acknowledgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve conflicts between reviewers’ requests and journal guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers' requests conflict with journal guidelines, authors should balance reviewer suggestions with the authors' original vision and seek editorial approval when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical organization and presentation of revisions while respecting journal policies. If a reviewer asks for changes that contradict journal scope or instructions, contact the editor for direction before making potentially inappropriate changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document revisions and perform final review
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoroughly revise the manuscript, document all changes, communicate clearly in the response, and perform a final review before resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize professionalism and attention to detail in documentation and communication. The section recommends reducing repetitive focus on gratitude and ensuring that the response and manuscript are carefully checked (including referencing appendix and limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use AI tools cautiously for proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are advised to use artificial intelligence tools as a supplementary measure, rather than a primary one, because such tools may not catch all linguistic nuances or contextual errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI tools can assist with proofreading but may miss contextual issues; do not rely on them as the sole method for language or content checks. Include a brief discussion of the limitations of AI tools and prefer human review for nuanced issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consume reviewers’ critiques (read, reflect, then respond)
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully read reviewers' comments, take time to reflect, and then craft responses rather than reacting immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that responding can be stressful; pausing before responding helps maintain objectivity and professionalism. The manuscript advises taking a moment to reflect before answering, especially to challenging critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize examples of major and minor reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Major comments include modifying the central hypothesis, changing the main algorithm, or redoing an experiment. Minor remarks include unclear statements, missing/incorrect references, unclear data presentation, grammatical concerns, reformulation, or adding small elements (paragraph/table/figure/appendix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these examples to categorize and prioritize reviewer feedback: address methodological or conceptual changes before minor edits like grammar or additional citations. Example major comment: 'the central hypothesis of the study needs to be revised to better align with the presented data.' Example minor comment: 'the introduction section would benefit from the inclusion of recent references...'
